title: Multicolor nonlinear chiral quantum optics: beyond phase
authors: Cedric Dufresne, Annabelle Makowski, Nir Rotenberg
abstract: Chiral quantum nonlinearities that arise when light interacts with quantum emitters are known to modulate only the phase but not the amplitude of scattered photons, enabling the creation of non-reciprocal photonic elements, quantum logic gates, and quantum network protocols. In this work, we show that the addition of a second photon beam drastically changes this picture, enabling both phase and amplitude modulation. Surprisingly, coherent photon transfer between the different beams enables a stronger amplitude modulation than standard symmetric interactions. This is most obvious in the coherent, three-photon amplification, which we predict peaks with a 30% efficiency in a chiral geometry, 3x the efficiency of the symmetric configuration. Our results uncover a new regime of chiral quantum optics and provide a route towards more efficient all-optical control at few-photon energies.
summary: This theoretical paper explores nonlinear chiral quantum optics by introducing a second photon beam to control emitter interactions. The authors demonstrate that chirality allows for strong amplitude modulation, enabling coherent three-photon amplification efficiencies up to 30%. This reveals a new regime for all-optical control at few-photon energies.
main_problem: To investigate chiral quantum nonlinear optics beyond simple phase modulation, demonstrating that adding a second photon beam enables both phase and amplitude modulation.
main_result: Chiral interactions allow for strong amplitude modulation via coherent energy transfer, predicting three-photon amplification efficiencies up to 30%, which is significantly higher than symmetric configurations.
method: The study uses the Green function formalism and Bloch equations, approximating by separating signal and control fields when one beam is much stronger than the other.
model_or_system:
The system involves quantum emitters interacting with two counter-propagating photon beams (signal and control) in both chiral ($ eta_L 
eq  eta_R$) and symmetric geometries.
key_observables: Phase shift ($\Delta\phi$), amplitude modulation ($\Delta T$ or $\Delta A$), and three-photon amplification efficiency.
important_parameters: Control beam power ($\Omega_c$), signal detuning ($\Delta$), and the ratio of coupling efficiencies defining chirality.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes an idealized case with no losses or noise, and employs a separation approximation for the signal and control fields.
figures_summary: Figures compare phase shift vs. amplitude modulation (Fig 1), show signal transmission spectra dependence on control power for chiral vs. symmetric cases (Fig 2), and plot control-power-dependent maximum extinction and three-photon amplification for both geometries (Figs 3 & 4).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the limitation of phase-only modulation in standard chiral setups, then introducing a second beam to enable amplitude control. It develops the theoretical framework using Green functions and Bloch equations, presenting results comparing the enhanced nonlinear effects (like three-photon amplification) found uniquely or more strongly in the chiral geometry.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses advanced quantum optics phenomena involving light-matter interaction, specifically exploring how engineered directional coupling (chirality) can enhance non-linear optical processes like few-photon amplification beyond what is achievable with standard symmetric interactions.
